---
title: Reference
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/reference
description: Event types, self-hosted worker CLI flags, supported MCP server types, rate limits, and branding guidelines for Claude Managed Agents.
---

This page collects reference material for Claude Managed Agents. For task-oriented guides, follow the links in each section. For the operations on the session resource, see [Session operations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/session-operations).

<Note>
  Managed Agents API requests require the `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta header, except memory store endpoints, which use `agent-memory-2026-07-22` instead. The SDK sets the correct beta header automatically. See [Beta headers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers#endpoint-specific-headers).
</Note>

## Event types

Persisted event type strings follow a `{domain}.{action}` naming convention; the stream-only event deltas (see the Event deltas tab) are the exception. See [Session event stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming) for sending, streaming, and listing events. Webhook event types are listed separately in [Subscribe to webhooks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks#supported-event-types), and some of their names differ from the stream's (for example, `session.status_idled` rather than `session.status_idle`).

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="User events">
    | Type                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
    | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `user.message`            | A user message with text, image, or document content.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
    | `user.interrupt`          | Stop the agent mid-execution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
    | `user.custom_tool_result` | Response to a custom tool call from the agent.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
    | `user.tool_confirmation`  | Approve or deny an agent or MCP tool call when a permission policy requires confirmation.                                                                                                                                                            |
    | `user.define_outcome`     | Define an [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) for the agent to work toward.                                                                                                                                |
    | `user.tool_result`        | For sessions with `self_hosted` [environments](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes) only, your integration is responsible for providing `agent_toolset` results. The SDK helpers and CLI do this automatically. |
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Agent events">
    | Type                             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
    | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    | `agent.message`                  | Agent response content blocks.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
    | `agent.thinking`                 | Signals the agent is making forward progress through extended thinking. This is a progress signal only and does not carry the thinking content.                                                                                                                                |
    | `agent.tool_use`                 | Agent invokes a pre-built agent tool (bash, file operations, and so on).                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
    | `agent.tool_result`              | Result of a pre-built agent tool execution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
    | `agent.mcp_tool_use`             | Agent invokes an MCP server tool.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
    | `agent.mcp_tool_result`          | Result of an MCP tool execution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
    | `agent.custom_tool_use`          | Agent invokes one of your custom tools. Respond with a `user.custom_tool_result` event.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
    | `agent.thread_context_compacted` | Conversation history was compacted to fit the context window.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
    | `agent.thread_message_received`  | In a [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session, a message from another thread arrived on the thread whose stream carries this event; on the primary thread, an agent sent a report or question to the coordinator.     |
    | `agent.thread_message_sent`      | In a [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) session, the thread whose stream carries this event sent a message to another thread; on the primary thread, the coordinator sent a task or follow-up message to another agent. |

    Message content in these events can include a `redacted` content block, `{"type": "redacted"}`: a placeholder for content withheld by Anthropic model policy. The block carries no other fields. Redacted blocks appear only in content the platform emits; a user event that includes one is rejected with a 400 error.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Session events">
    | Type                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
    | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `session.status_running`            | Agent is actively processing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
    | `session.status_idle`               | Agent finished its current task and is waiting for input. Includes a `stop_reason` indicating why the agent stopped.                                                                                                                                            |
    | `session.status_rescheduled`        | A transient error occurred and the session is retrying automatically.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
    | `session.status_terminated`         | Session ended, either because of an unrecoverable error or because it was archived.                                                                                                                                                                             |
    | `session.deleted`                   | Session was deleted. Terminates any active event stream; no further events are emitted for this session.                                                                                                                                                        |
    | `session.updated`                   | Session update request changed at least one field. Includes only the fields that changed. Updates apply on the next turn.                                                                                                                                       |
    | `session.error`                     | An error occurred during processing. Includes a typed `error` object with a `retry_status`.                                                                                                                                                                     |
    | `session.usage`                     | Snapshot of the session's cumulative usage and tracked list cost. Carries the session's usage totals and an echo of the session's [budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets), or `null` when the session has none.                    |
    | `session.thread_created`            | A [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) thread was created.                                                                                                                                                 |
    | `session.thread_status_running`     | A session thread began executing. Every session emits this for its primary thread; in [multiagent](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration) sessions, child-thread transitions are also cross-posted to the primary stream. |
    | `session.thread_status_idle`        | A session thread finished its turn and is awaiting input. Includes `stop_reason`.                                                                                                                                                                               |
    | `session.thread_status_rescheduled` | A session thread hit a transient error and is retrying automatically.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
    | `session.thread_status_terminated`  | A session thread was archived or reached a terminal error.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Span events">
    Span events are observability markers that wrap activity for timing and usage tracking.

    | Type                              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
    | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    | `span.model_request_start`        | A model inference call has started.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
    | `span.model_request_end`          | A model inference call has completed. Includes `model_usage` with token counts.                                                                                                                                                                          |
    | `span.outcome_evaluation_start`   | [Outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation has started.                                                                                                                                                    |
    | `span.outcome_evaluation_ongoing` | Heartbeat during an ongoing [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation.                                                                                                                                    |
    | `span.outcome_evaluation_end`     | An [outcome](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/define-outcomes) evaluation cycle has completed. A `needs_revision` result means another cycle follows; `satisfied`, `max_iterations_reached`, `failed`, and `interrupted` are terminal. |
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="System events">
    | Type             | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
    | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    | `system.message` | Append privileged system-level context that applies to the accompanying turn and all subsequent turns. Supported on Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Mythos 5, Claude Opus 5, and Claude Opus 4.8. On an unsupported primary model the event is rejected with `model_does_not_support_mid_conversation_system`. |
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Event deltas">
    Event deltas are stream-only preview events. They are emitted on stream connections (session-level or per-thread) that opt in with the `event_deltas[]` parameter, and they are never persisted to the session's event history. See [Event deltas](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming#event-deltas) for opting in, accumulating, and reconciling them.

    | Type          | Description                                                                                                              |
    | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    | `event_start` | A previewed event has started generating. Carries the upcoming event's `type` and `id`. Stream-only and never persisted. |
    | `event_delta` | Incremental content for a previewed event, identified by `event_id`. Stream-only and never persisted.                    |
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Self-hosted worker

These are the `ant beta:worker` CLI flags for the pre-built worker that drives a `self_hosted` environment. See [Self-hosted sandboxes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes) for setting up the environment, running a worker, and the SDK helper options.

| Flag                   | Description                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--environment-id`     | The environment to poll for work. Also reads from `ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_ID`.                                                                                                         |
| `--environment-key`    | Authenticates the worker with this environment. Also reads from `ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY`.                                                                                          |
| `--workdir`            | Directory where skills are downloaded and tools read and write files. Defaults to `.` (the current directory); the system default working directory is `/workspace`.                  |
| `--on-work`            | Script to call for each claimed work item instead of running tools in-process. Receives session details as environment variables.                                                     |
| `--unrestricted-paths` | Allow the file tools to read and write paths outside `--workdir`. The workdir check is a guardrail for the file tools only, not a sandbox; it does not constrain bash.                |
| `--max-idle`           | How long to wait after the session goes idle with an `end_turn` [stop reason](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/handling-stop-reasons) before shutting down. Defaults to `60s`. |
| `--log-format`         | Log output format. Use `json` for structured log ingestion. Defaults to `text`.                                                                                                       |

The CLI worker does not mount [memory stores](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory): a session that attaches one still runs, but the agent finds nothing at the store's `mount_path` and no changes sync back to the store. To use memory stores in sessions on a self-hosted environment, run the SDK worker instead; see [Use memory stores](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/self-hosted-sandboxes#use-memory-stores).

## Supported MCP server types

Claude Managed Agents connects to [remote MCP servers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/remote-mcp-servers) that expose an HTTP endpoint, or to private MCP servers through [MCP tunnels](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-tunnels/overview). The server should support the MCP protocol's streamable HTTP transport; servers that only support the deprecated SSE transport still work through an automatic fallback. See [MCP connector](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/mcp-connector) for declaring servers on an agent.

For more information on MCP and building MCP servers, see the [MCP documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).

## Rate limits

Managed Agents endpoints are rate-limited per organization:

| Operation                                                     | Limit                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Create endpoints (such as agents, sessions, and environments) | 300 requests per minute   |
| Read endpoints (such as retrieve, list, and stream)           | 1,200 requests per minute |

Organization-level [spend limits and usage-tier rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/rate-limits) also apply.

## Branding guidelines

For partners integrating Claude Managed Agents, use of Claude branding is optional. When referencing Claude in your product:

**Allowed:**

* "Claude Agent" (preferred for dropdown menus)
* "Claude" (when within a menu already labeled "Agents")
* "\{YourAgentName} Powered by Claude" (if you have an existing agent name)

**Not permitted:**

* "Claude Code" or "Claude Code Agent"
* "Claude Cowork" or "Claude Cowork Agent"
* Claude Code-branded ASCII art or visual elements that mimic Claude Code

Your product should maintain its own branding and not appear to be Claude Code, Claude Cowork, or any other Anthropic product. For questions about branding compliance, contact the Anthropic [sales team](https://www.anthropic.com/contact-sales).

# ADK 2.0 Key Information

**Release Dates:**
- Python: May 19, 2026
- Go: June 30, 2026
- TypeScript: August 21, 2026

**License:** The documentation repository uses an open-source license available at github.com/google/adk-docs/blob/main/LICENSE

**Workflow Runtime & Graph Execution:**
ADK 2.0 transitions from hierarchical agent execution to "a graph-based execution engine" where agents, tools, and functions operate as individual nodes within a workflow graph.

**Parallel/Fan-Out Agents:**
The framework supports parallel workflows. Deprecated 1.x template classes exist (SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent), with migration guidance recommending graph workflows as replacements.

**Human-in-the-Loop:**
The system includes "Human input" capabilities for workflows and supports pausing for human intervention through RequestedInput signaling in the event schema.

**Evaluation Features:**
Evaluation tools include criteria-based assessment, user simulation, environment simulation, custom metrics, and optimization capabilities.

**Resumability/Checkpointing:**
The framework supports agent resumption and cancellation through dedicated runtime features.

**A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Support:**
Full A2A protocol implementation exists with quickstart guides for exposing and consuming agent capabilities across Python, Go, Java, and Kotlin.

## Human-in-the-Loop Features

The release introduces HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) capabilities through the **HITLOperator**. Key use cases include:
- AI/ML model validation with human review of outputs
- Content moderation routing before publication
- Manager approval workflows for sensitive operations
- Data quality validation by stewards

- Reference points (DAG queued time, logical date, or fixed datetime)

While Airflow 3.1.0 doesn't directly introduce AI agents, the release notes reference a separate **Common AI Provider** (announced April 2026) that "adds LLM and AI agent operators to Apache Airflow with 6 operators, 5 toolsets, and 20+ model providers."

The 3.1.0 release also enables the **Inference Execution** API endpoint for real-time workflow integration, supporting responsive patterns for AI/ML pipelines.

> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt

# Agent SDK overview

> Build production AI agents with Claude Code as a library

An agent is an application that completes a task by planning its own steps and calling tools that read files, run commands, or edit code. The Agent SDK gives you the same tools, [agent loop](/docs/en/agent-sdk/agent-loop), and context management that power Claude Code, programmable in Python and TypeScript.

## Compare the Agent SDK to other Claude tools

The Agent SDK, the CLI, the Client SDK, and Managed Agents each fit different needs. Use the table to find the one that matches what you're building.

| If you're...                                                                                            | Use                                                                               | Why                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Building an agent without implementing the tool loop yourself                                           | **Agent SDK**                                                                     | A library that runs the agent loop in your own process, in Python or TypeScript.                     |
| Doing interactive development or running one-off tasks from a terminal                                  | [**Claude Code CLI**](/docs/en/overview)                                               | The terminal interface, built for daily interactive use.                                             |
| Calling the API directly and implementing the tool loop yourself                                        | [**Client SDK**](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/client-sdks)             | Direct access to the Anthropic API rather than to Claude Code. You implement the tool loop yourself. |
| Running long-running or asynchronous agents without managing your own sandbox or session infrastructure | [**Managed Agents**](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview) | Hosted REST API, a separate product from the Agent SDK. Anthropic runs the agent and the sandbox.    |

The SDK is available as a library for Python and TypeScript only. To drive the same agent loop from another language, [run the CLI as a subprocess](/docs/en/headless) with the `-p` flag and `--output-format json`.

## Capabilities

These Claude Code capabilities are available in the SDK:

| Capability                   | What it does                                                                                 | Learn more                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Built-in tools               | Read, write, edit files, run commands, and search the web                                    | [Tools reference](/docs/en/tools-reference)                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Hooks                        | Run custom code at key points in the agent lifecycle                                         | [Hooks](/docs/en/agent-sdk/hooks)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Subagents                    | Spawn specialized agents for focused subtasks                                                | [Subagents](/docs/en/agent-sdk/subagents)                                                                                                                                                                           |
| MCP                          | Connect external tools and data sources via the Model Context Protocol                       | [MCP](/docs/en/agent-sdk/mcp)                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Permissions                  | Control which tools run automatically, which need approval                                   | [Permissions](/docs/en/agent-sdk/permissions)                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Sessions                     | Maintain context across exchanges, resume or fork later                                      | [Sessions](/docs/en/agent-sdk/sessions)                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Skills, commands, and memory | Load automatically from your project's `.claude/` and from `~/.claude/`, same as Claude Code | [Skills](/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills), [Commands](/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills#commands-in-agent-sdk-sessions), [Memory](/docs/en/agent-sdk/modifying-system-prompts), [Configuration loading](/docs/en/agent-sdk/claude-code-features) |
| Plugins                      | Package skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers, and load them by local path                  | [Plugins](/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins)                                                                                                                                                                               |

## Get started

Follow the [Quickstart](/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart) to install the SDK, set your API key, and build your first agent, one that finds and fixes bugs in existing code.

<Note>
  Unless previously approved, Anthropic does not allow third party developers to offer claude.ai login or rate limits for their products, including agents built on the Claude Agent SDK. Use the API key authentication methods described in the [Quickstart](/docs/en/agent-sdk/quickstart) instead.
</Note>

## Changelog

View the full changelog for SDK updates, bug fixes, and new features:

* **TypeScript SDK**: [view CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
* **Python SDK**: [view CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Report bugs

If you encounter bugs or issues with the Agent SDK:

* **TypeScript SDK**: [report issues on GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-typescript/issues)
* **Python SDK**: [report issues on GitHub](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/issues)

## Branding guidelines

For partners integrating the Claude Agent SDK, use of Claude branding is optional. When referencing Claude in your product:

**Allowed:**

* "Claude Agent", preferred for dropdown menus
* "Claude", when within a menu already labeled "Agents"
* "\{YourAgentName} Powered by Claude", if you have an existing agent name

**Not permitted:**

* "Claude Code" or "Claude Code Agent"
* Claude Code-branded ASCII art or visual elements that mimic Claude Code

Your product should maintain its own branding and not appear to be Claude Code or any Anthropic product. For questions about branding compliance, contact the Anthropic [sales team](https://www.anthropic.com/contact-sales).

## License and terms

Use of the Claude Agent SDK is governed by [Anthropic's Commercial Terms of Service](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms), including when you use it to power products and services that you make available to your own customers and end users, except to the extent a specific component or dependency is covered by a different license as indicated in that component's LICENSE file.

## Next steps

description: Coordinate multiple agents within a single session.

Multiagent orchestration lets one agent coordinate with others to complete complex work. Agents can act in parallel with their own isolated context, which helps improve output quality and can also improve time to completion.

Not sure a multiagent setup fits your problem? See [when to use multiagent systems (and when not to)](https://claude.com/blog/building-multi-agent-systems-when-and-how-to-use-them).

<Note>

The SDK sets the correct beta header automatically. See [Beta headers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers#endpoint-specific-headers).
</Note>

## How it works

All agents share the same sandbox, filesystem, and [vault credentials](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/vaults), but each agent runs in its own **session thread**, a context-isolated event stream with its own conversation history. The coordinator reports activity in the **primary thread** (which is the same as the session-level [event stream](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/events-and-streaming)); additional threads are spawned at runtime when the coordinator delegates work.

Threads are persistent: the coordinator can send a follow-up to an agent it called earlier, and that agent retains everything from its previous turns.

Each agent uses its own configuration: model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers, and skills. Session-level [agent configuration overrides](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/sessions#override-agent-configuration-for-a-session) are the exception; they apply to the coordinator and its `self` copies. Tools, MCP servers, and context are not shared.

# Human-in-the-Loop in OpenAI Agents SDK

## Tool Approval Mechanism

Tools declare approval requirements via the `needs_approval` parameter, which accepts either a boolean or an async function. The callable receives run context, tool parameters, and call ID to make per-call decisions. As documented: "Set `needs_approval` to `True` to always require approval or provide an async function that decides per call."

## Interruption Flow

When a tool requires approval without a stored decision, execution pauses and surfaces `ToolApprovalItem` entries in `RunResult.interruptions`. These interruptions include agent name, tool name, and arguments. The system handles approvals consistently whether they originate from the current agent, handoffs, or nested `Agent.as_tool()` executions—all surface on the outer run.

## State Serialization & Resumption

Paused runs convert to `RunState` via `result.to_state()`. Developers can then persist this state using `to_json()` or `to_string()`, store it externally, reload it with `RunState.from_json()` or `RunState.from_string()`, and resume execution with `Runner.run(agent, state)`. Approval decisions persist through serialization when marked with `always_approve=True` or `always_reject=True`.

## Durable Execution

The documentation emphasizes that "RunState is designed to be durable," supporting storage in databases or queues. Optional parameters like `context_serializer`, `context_deserializer`, and `strict_context=True` enable customization. However, **no mention of Temporal or other distributed workflow platforms appears in this documentation**.

## Key Limitation

The documentation does not address specific scalability limits for pending approvals or integration with external orchestration systems.

# Key Extracts from "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?"

## Dataset Size
MAST-Data comprises **1,642 annotated execution traces** collected across multiple multi-agent frameworks.

## Seven Frameworks Evaluated
1. ChatDev
2. MetaGPT
3. HyperAgent
4. AppWorld
5. AG2 (MathChat)
6. Magentic-One
7. OpenManus

## 14 Failure Modes by Category

**FC1: System Design Issues (5 modes)**
- FM-1.1: Disobey task specification (11.8%)
- FM-1.2: Disobey role specification (1.5%)
- FM-1.3: Step repetition (15.7%)
- FM-1.4: Loss of conversation history (2.80%)
- FM-1.5: Unaware of stopping conditions (12.4%)

**FC2: Inter-Agent Misalignment (6 modes)**
- FM-2.1: Conversation reset (2.20%)
- FM-2.2: Fail to ask for clarification (6.80%)
- FM-2.3: Task derailment (7.40%)
- FM-2.4: Information withholding (0.85%)
- FM-2.5: Ignored other agent's input (1.90%)
- FM-2.6: Reasoning-action mismatch (13.2%)

**FC3: Task Verification (3 modes)**
- FM-3.1: Premature termination (6.20%)
- FM-3.2: No or incomplete verification (8.20%)
- FM-3.3: Incorrect verification (9.10%)

## Annotation Agreement Metrics
The LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline achieved **94% accuracy and Cohen's Kappa of 0.77** when compared to human expert annotations on held-out validation sets.

## Intervention Results

**AG2 - MathChat Case Study:**
Adding structured verification sections yielded improvements, though specific percentage gains weren't detailed separately in the main text.

**ChatDev Case Study:**
- Workflow adjustments ensuring CEO agent final approval: **+9.4% success rate increase**
- Adding high-level task objective verification step: **+15.6% improvement** on ProgramDev benchmark

## Publication Status
This work appears as arXiv:2503.13657v3, dated October 26, 2025. No traditional venue acceptance is noted; it remains an arXiv preprint.

# Subagents: Configuration, Execution, and Constraints

## Definition and Configuration

Subagents are defined as **Markdown files with YAML frontmatter** in one of these scopes:

- **`.claude/agents/`** – Project-level (highest priority after managed settings)
- **`~/.claude/agents/`** – User-level (personal, available across all projects)
- **`--agents` CLI flag** – Session-only (JSON format)
- **Managed settings** – Organization-wide
- **Plugins** – Plugin-provided agents

### Required Frontmatter Fields

Only `name` and `description` are required:

```yaml
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Reviews code for quality and best practices
tools: Read, Glob, Grep
model: sonnet
---

You are a code reviewer. When invoked, analyze the code and provide
specific, actionable feedback on quality, security, and best practices.
```

## Parallel Execution and Concurrency Limits

### Parallel Execution
Subagents **can run in parallel**. Claude spawns multiple subagents to work simultaneously on independent tasks:

```text
Research the authentication, database, and API modules in parallel using separate subagents
```

### Concurrent Subagent Limit

**Default: 20 concurrent subagents maximum**

> "By default, when 20 subagents are running in a session, spawning another with the Agent tool fails with `Concurrent subagent limit reached`"

This limit is controlled by:
```
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS
```

The limit can be changed to any positive whole number:
```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS": "50"
  }
}
```

**Exceptions:**
- Sessions with [ultracode](/docs/en/model-config#adjust-effort-level) active are exempt
- This only blocks subagents Claude spawns via the `Agent` tool
- Resuming completed subagents doesn't check the limit
- Agent team teammates and workflow agents follow their own limits

## Nesting: Subagents Spawning Subagents

### Default Nesting Depth

Subagents **can spawn their own subagents** up to a default limit of **3 layers below the main conversation**:

> "By default, a subagent can spawn subagents of its own, up to three layers below the main conversation. At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork"

### Controlling Nesting Depth

Configure with `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH": "2"
  }
}
```

- **Value `1`** – Turn nesting off entirely
- **Value `2`** – Allow subagents to delegate to a second layer only
- **Value `3`** – Default (current)

> "At the depth limit, Claude Code withholds the `Agent` tool from every subagent except a fork, so a subagent at the limit does its delegated work itself and returns one summary."

## Context Isolation

Subagents start with **isolated, fresh context** except for forks:

### Non-Fork Subagent Context Includes:
- System prompt (agent's own, not Claude Code's default)
- Task message from Claude
- CLAUDE.md files (except Explore and Plan)
- Git status snapshot (except Explore and Plan)
- Preloaded skills (if listed in `skills` field)
- Sibling roster (list of named agents)

### What's Excluded:
- Conversation history
- Output style preferences
- Main conversation's auto memory
- Previous file reads or skill invocations

**Forks are the exception:** They inherit the entire parent conversation context, system prompt, tools, model, and message history.

## Tool Restrictions

### Available Tools Framework

Subagents inherit built-in and MCP tools, filtered by:

1. **Universal removal** – These tools are never available to any subagent:
   - `Agent` (at depth limit)
   - `AskUserQuestion`
   - `EndConversation`
   - `EnterPlanMode`
   - `ExitPlanMode` (except in plan mode)
   - `ScheduleWakeup`
   - `Workflow`

2. **Background subagent filter** – Background subagents (default) only keep:
   - `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Bash`, `PowerShell`, `Edit`, `Write`, `NotebookEdit`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `TodoWrite`, `Skill`, `ToolSearch`, `EnterWorktree`, `ExitWorktree`, `Monitor`, `TaskStop`, `SendMessage`
   - All MCP tools

### Restricting Tools via Configuration

Use `tools` as an allowlist:
```yaml
---
name: safe-researcher
description: Research agent with restricted capabilities
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
---
```

Or `disallowedTools` as a denylist:
```yaml
---
name: no-writes
description: Inherits available tools except file writes
disallowedTools: Write, Edit
---
```

Use MCP patterns to restrict server tools:
```yaml
disallowedTools: mcp__github  # Remove all github server tools
```

### Restrict Spawnable Subagent Types

When running as main thread (`claude --agent`), restrict which subagents can be spawned:
```yaml
tools: Agent(worker, researcher), Read, Bash
```

This is an allowlist—only `worker` and `researcher` can be spawned.

## Permission Modes

Subagents can run in different permission modes via `permissionMode`:

| Mode | Behavior |
|------|----------|
| `default` | Manual mode: prompts for permission |
| `acceptEdits` | Auto-accept file edits and filesystem commands |
| `auto` | [Auto mode](/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode): classifier reviews commands |
| `dontAsk` | Auto-deny prompts; explicit allows still work |
| `bypassPermissions` | Skip all permission prompts |
| `plan` | Plan mode (read-only) |

```yaml
---
name: db-reader
description: Execute read-only database queries
permissionMode: plan
---
```

**Important:** If the parent uses `bypassPermissions` or `acceptEdits`, this takes precedence and can't be overridden.

## Hooks: Lifecycle Control

### Frontmatter Hooks (Subagent-Specific)

Define in the subagent's markdown file:

```yaml
---
name: code-reviewer
description: Review code changes with automatic linting
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Bash"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "./scripts/validate-command.sh"
  PostToolUse:
    - matcher: "Edit|Write"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "./scripts/run-linter.sh"
---
```

Supported events:
- `PreToolUse` – Before tool use
- `PostToolUse` – After tool use
- `Stop` – When subagent finishes

### Session-Wide Hooks

Configure in `settings.json` to respond to subagent lifecycle:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SubagentStart": [
      {
        "matcher": "db-agent",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "./scripts/setup-db-connection.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "SubagentStop": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "./scripts/cleanup-db-connection.sh" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Additional Constraints

### Description Token Limit
> "When the combined descriptions of your subagents, except the built-in ones, exceed 15,000 tokens, Claude Code shows a warning at startup"

### Max Turns Limit
```yaml
---
name: repo-auditor
description: Audits a repository
maxTurns: 10
---
```
When reached, the subagent's output is marked partial and can be resumed.

### Isolation Option
Run a subagent in an isolated git worktree:
```yaml
isolation: worktree
```

259:* `{"type": "advisor", "model": "<model id>"}` gives the session's primary thread an advisor it can consult mid-turn. At most one advisor entry per roster. See [Give the session an advisor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#give-the-session-an-advisor).
265:The coordinator can only delegate to one level of agents; referencing an agent that has its own `multiagent.agents` roster fails the create or update request with a validation error. A maximum of 20 unique agents can be listed in `multiagent.agents`, but the coordinator can call multiple copies of each agent.
292:A roster can contain at most one advisor entry, alongside any of the other roster forms. The entry occupies the reserved roster name `anthropic.advisor`: a roster that lists both an advisor entry and a member literally named `anthropic.advisor` is rejected with a 400 validation error. In responses, the advisor entry is echoed last in the roster regardless of the position it was submitted in.
318:Advisor threads are exempt from the concurrent-thread limit. They appear in the session's [thread list](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#threads) with `agent` set to the advisor form exactly as configured (`{"type": "advisor", "model": ...}`) and `parent_thread_id` set to the primary thread.
414:* To limit an agent's access, declare only the servers it needs in its agent definition.
794:A [session budget](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/budgets) is a single shared cap across all of a session's threads. As the cap is reached, threads pause independently, and each thread's cost is priced at the thread's own served model.
797:  A maximum of 25 concurrent threads is supported. The coordinator can call multiple copies of a single agent in the roster, creating multiple threads associated with one `agent`. [Advisor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/multiagent-orchestration#give-the-session-an-advisor) consultation threads are exempt from this limit.
960:    Optionally archive a session thread when it has completed its work. This frees up a thread against the 25-thread limit.

content.content:
# Multi-Agent Systems: Key Guidance from Claude Blog

**Publication Date:** January 23, 2026

## When Multi-Agent Systems Help

Three consistent scenarios where multiple agents outperform single agents:

1. **Context Protection**: "When an agent's context accumulates information from one subtask that is irrelevant to subsequent subtasks, context pollution occurs."

2. **Parallelization**: Tasks decomposing into independent pieces enable concurrent exploration of larger information spaces.

3. **Specialization**: Different tool sets, system prompts, or domain expertise improve reliability when agents have focused responsibilities.

## When They Hurt

The article warns against multi-agent complexity without genuine constraints. Teams frequently build elaborate architectures that underperform: "we've seen teams invest months building elaborate multi-agent architectures only to discover that improved prompting on a single agent achieved equivalent results."

## Cost & Token Implications

Quantified overhead: "multi-agent implementations typically use 3-10x more tokens than single-agent approaches for equivalent tasks." The overhead stems from "duplicating context across agents, coordination messages between agents, and summarizing results for handoffs."

## Coordinator Pattern

The article emphasizes the **orchestrator-subagent hierarchical model**: a lead agent spawns and manages specialized subagents for specific subtasks. Critically, work should follow "context-centric decomposition" rather than problem-type division to minimize coordination losses.

## Key Guidance

Start simple: "Start with the simplest approach that works, and add complexity only when evidence supports it."

# Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code: Publication Date and Key Mechanisms

**Publication Date:** June 2, 2026

## Key Orchestration Mechanisms

**Workflow Scripts:**
Dynamic workflows execute JavaScript files with special functions to "spawn and coordinate subagents." Standard JavaScript functions like JSON, Math, and Array help process data.

**Fan-Out Pattern:**
Claude can "split up a task into many smaller steps, run an agent on each step and then synthesize those results," particularly useful when "each step benefits from its own clean context window."

**Resume Capability:**
"If a workflow is interrupted, for example by user action or quitting the terminal, resuming the session will allow the workflow to pick up where it left off."

**Scoring & Verification:**
The article describes "adversarial verification" where separate spawned agents verify output against rubrics, and "tournament" patterns where "N agents each attempt the same task using different approaches" with pairwise judging.

## Quantitative Data

The article provides **no specific numbers** on:
- Subagent counts per workflow
- Token usage costs
- Success rates or performance metrics

The only contextual hint: "don't use resource intensive commands so that you can maximally parallelize without running out of resources on your machine."

# OrchestraBench Paper Summary

**What OrchestraBench Measures:**
The benchmark evaluates "failure, recovery, and decomposition through a controlled, seed-reproducible failure-injection harness" across multi-agent systems. Primary metrics include cascade radius and per-failure-mode recovery rates.

**Frameworks/Orchestration Patterns:**
The study examined routing policies, comparing keyword/flag routers against intent-reasoning model routers. Testing involved Claude agents across three model sizes (Sonnet, Opus, Haiku).

**Number of Tasks:**
The evaluation included a 26-case gold-labeled diagnostic dataset with controlled mechanism probes over arithmetic dependency chains and loan-approval workflow reframings.

**Key Quantitative Findings:**
- Keyword/flag router: 0% on adversarial cases
- Intent-reasoning router: 100% accuracy matching oracle performance
- Recovery tiers: tool faults recovered fully (1.0), ambiguous delegation partially (0.30), latent/semantic modes never recovered (0.0)
- Cascade radius increased from 0.9 to 4.7 across pipeline depths of 3-7

# Analysis of arXiv Paper 2608.03836

## Frameworks Examined
The abstract mentions "Five widely deployed agent workflow frameworks" but **names only three specifically**: LangGraph 1.2.9, CrewAI 1.15.2, and pydantic-graph 1.x. The other two frameworks are not identified in the provided abstract.

## Key Findings
The paper documents serious conformance failures:

- **LangGraph 1.2.9**: "durably records a second resume value and never consults it" and "re-executes durably recorded work after a real SIGKILL"

- **CrewAI 1.15.2**: Re-executes completed methods contrary to documented behavior

- **pydantic-graph 1.x**: Cannot resume after mid-node crashes

- **Concurrent consumption failure**: "k processes resuming one parked interrupt fire the gated effect k times" with "saturation 1.0 in 36 of 40 cells"

## Proposed Contract
The RESUME CONTRACT specifies "six properties over the persistence API (prefix continuation, effect exactly-once, fork determinism, checkpoint validity, consume-once, recovery determinism)"

## Author Affiliation & Date
**Author**: Sajjad Khan

**Affiliation**: Not provided in the abstract

**Submission Date**: August 4, 2026 (v1); final revision August 8, 2026 (v3)

# Paper Summary: Failure Localization in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems

**Core Task:** The research addresses identifying which agent caused system failures and the specific step where trajectories became irreversibly misdirected in LLM-based multi-agent systems.

**Framework:** AgentLocate combines "an LLM-based judging mechanism with multi-perspective verification by independent evaluators" whose assessments use confidence-aware aggregation and lightweight fine-tuning.

**Key Results:** The framework "consistently outperforms existing failure localization methods in identifying both responsible agents and failure steps, while remaining efficient in terms of token usage and running time."

# Scaling Behavior of Single LLM-Driven Multi-Agent Systems - Key Findings

## Scaling Findings
The research demonstrates that performance in homogeneous multi-agent systems does not improve linearly with agent count. Instead, the work reveals "a pattern of diminishing returns, governed by a trade-off between collaborative synergy and coordination overhead." The authors establish that task type significantly influences the optimal number of agents, and that having sufficient base LLM capability is essential for effectiveness.

## Performance Degradation
Notably, performance decline stems from "coordination overhead rather than merely long-context failure," and this scaling pattern holds across different interaction architectures, including structured debate topologies.

## Authors
- Jialing Li
- Zhouhong Gu
- Yin Cai
- Hongwei Feng

## Publication Details
- **arXiv ID:** 2606.00655
- **Submission Date:** May 30, 2026
- **Category:** Multiagent Systems (cs.MA)

## Methodology
The authors introduced the Sequential Iterative Multi-Agent System (SIMAS) framework to isolate collaboration effects while examining scaling behavior across diverse tasks and model sizes.

# LangGraph Persistence: Checkpointers and Thread Management

## Core Concepts

**Checkpointers** persist graph state snapshots within a single thread, enabling short-term memory. The documentation describes them as tools for "conversation continuity, human-in-the-loop workflows, time travel, and fault tolerance."

A thread represents a continuous conversation or interaction session. When you invoke a graph, you pass a `thread_id` in the configuration to establish which thread the execution belongs to. This allows the system to retrieve previous state checkpoints for that specific thread.

## Supported Backends

The page mentions three persistent checkpointer implementations:

1. **PostgresSaver** – PostgreSQL database with async support
2. **SqliteSaver** – Local file-based storage suitable for development
3. **InMemorySaver** – RAM-based (non-persistent between restarts)

The documentation also references that other backends like Redis and MongoDB exist but provides no details about them in this excerpt.

## Time Travel and Interrupts

The guide identifies "time travel" as a checkpointer use case, though specific mechanics aren't explained here. Similarly, human-in-the-loop workflows are mentioned as a key persistence benefit, but implementation details aren't provided in this section.

## Key Limitation

"MemorySaver and InMemorySaver store checkpoints in RAM. When the process restarts, all checkpoints are lost," making them unsuitable for production persistence needs.

# Braintrust Self-Hosting Overview

## Deployment Model
Braintrust uses a hybrid architecture where the **control plane** (web UI, authentication, user management) is hosted by Braintrust, while customers deploy the **data plane** (API, database, storage, query engine) in their own infrastructure.

## Supported Cloud Providers
Official Terraform modules are available for:
- **AWS** (ECS and EC2)
- **Google Cloud Platform** (Kubernetes and Helm)
- **Azure** (Kubernetes and Helm)

Note: The documentation does not mention Vercel as a supported provider for self-hosting.

## Data Residency in Customer VPC
All sensitive AI data remains in the customer's self-hosted data plane, including:
- "Experiment records (input, output, expected, scores, metadata, traces, spans)"
- Dataset records and logs
- Prompt playground data
- Project-level LLM provider secrets (encrypted)

The control plane stores only metadata (project names, organization settings, API keys) and does not access sensitive data.

## Plan Requirement
"Self-hosting is only available on the Enterprise plan."

# Human Input in CrewAI

## How Human Input Works

Based on the documentation, CrewAI integrates human input through a straightforward mechanism:

**The `human_input` flag:** Set `human_input=True` in a Task definition to enable this feature. When activated, the agent pauses execution and prompts the user for input before delivering its final answer.

**Purpose:** As stated in the docs, this feature is "especially useful in complex decision-making processes or when agents require more details to complete a task effectively." The human input can provide additional context, resolve ambiguities, or validate agent outputs.

## What's NOT Mentioned

The provided documentation excerpt **does not cover**:

- AMP/enterprise HITL (Human-in-the-Loop) features via webhooks
- Evaluation or tracing capabilities
- Advanced monitoring or approval workflows beyond basic human prompts

The example demonstrates two tasks with `human_input=True`, where the researcher agent asks for human confirmation on draft quality, and the writer agent requests input before finalizing the blog post.

**License Name & Version:** Sustainable Use License, Version 1.0

## Permitted Uses

The license grants rights for **internal business purposes** and **non-commercial/personal use**. You may "use, copy, distribute, make available, and prepare derivative works" subject to stated limitations.

Commercial distribution is restricted. The license explicitly states: "You may not...alter, remove, or obscure any licensing, copyright, or other notices." Additionally, you cannot distribute the software for commercial gain—sharing is limited to non-commercial contexts only.

## Enterprise Edition (.ee) Files

Files containing ".ee." in filenames or ".ee" in directory paths operate under a **separate licensing regime**. These components require "a valid n8n Enterprise License specifically allowing you access to such source code files," as detailed in a separate LICENSE_EE.md document. Standard Sustainable Use License terms do not apply to these restricted files.

The agreement includes automatic termination language: violations result in immediate license loss, though reinstatement is possible within 30 days of ceasing violations.

# Research Summary

**Paper:** arXiv:2605.22502, submitted May 21, 2026

**Authors:** Simon Dennis, Rivaan Patil, Kevin Shabahang, Hao Guo (affiliations not specified in provided content)

## Agent Orchestration Frameworks
The abstract identifies seven major frameworks with collective GitHub presence: "LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Semantic Kernel, Strands, and LlamaIndex," totaling over 290,000 stars. These typically use external orchestrators positioned above the LLM.

## Proposed Method
Rather than external orchestration, the researchers propose "compiling the procedure into the weights of a small fine-tuned model" (termed a "subterranean agent"). This embeds workflow logic directly within model parameters via fine-tuning.

## Quantitative Claims
The paper asserts achieving "near-frontier quality at two orders of magnitude less cost"—a 100x cost reduction while maintaining performance comparable to frontier models.

## Testing Scope
The researchers validated their approach across three scenarios: travel booking (14 nodes), Zoom support with product-specific knowledge (14 nodes), and insurance claims processing (55 nodes with 6 decision hubs).

# Human-in-the-Loop in CrewAI AMP

Based on the provided documentation, I cannot extract the requested details about human-in-the-loop implementation. While the page includes a navigation link to "HITL Workflows" in the guides section, the actual content describing webhook-based pause mechanisms, resume endpoints, approval/feedback flows, timeouts, tracing, evaluations, or scoring features is **not included** in the source material provided.

Alternatively, the documentation index at `/llms.txt` may provide access to comprehensive HITL documentation.

Based on the provided documentation, I cannot find specific pricing information for Memory Bank services. The page references pricing sections but does not display:

- **Price per 1,000 memories or events**

The documentation mentions that "Agent Platform Memory Bank uses Generative AI models to generate memories" and that processing occurs "within the specific region or multi-region of the model endpoint," but specific regional availability is not listed on this scale overview page.

**Recommendation:** Check the dedicated Memory Bank setup documentation or the pricing page directly at cloud.google.com/products/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/pricing for current pricing details and regional availability.

# Open Agent Specification Summary

**What It Is:**
The Open Agent Specification (Agent Spec) is "a framework-agnostic declarative language for representing AI agents and workflows" that enables standardized comparison of agentic systems across different runtimes.

**Frameworks/Runtimes Compared:**
The research evaluated four distinct platforms: LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and WayFlow (a reference runtime developed by the authors).

**Key Performance Findings:**
- **SimpleQA Verified:** CrewAI achieved 81.1% F1 score versus WayFlow's 79.0%, despite using identical agent logic, indicating framework-specific trade-offs between accuracy and speed
- **τ²-Bench:** AutoGen showed 73.5% Pass rate while CrewAI achieved only 62.5% on the same specification, demonstrating significant variance from prompt handling differences
- **BIRD-SQL:** Performance was less framework-sensitive, with most runtimes around 54% accuracy for basic agents

**Authors' Affiliation:**
Oracle (the company name appears at the top of the author list)

**Submission Date:**
May 19, 2026

Pricing: the public pricing page rendered "$-" for hosted rates; the Azure Retail Prices API (queried 2026-09-04) lists "Foundry Agents / Hosted vCPU Usage" $0.10934/hour and "Hosted Memory Usage" $0.01298/GiB-hour in Sweden Central, Germany West Central, France Central, Italy North, Spain Central (East US $0.0994 and $0.0118); Short Term Memory $0.275/1k events; Long Term Memory $0.275/1k memories/month; Memory Retrievals $0.55/1k; Skills Execution Container $0.0363/hour. Reverse-engineer: immutable agent versions bound to a per-session sandbox whose filesystem survives idle deprovisioning — cheap "scale-to-zero with resume" for long agent runs.

**Temporal — Temporal Technologies.** Durable execution via deterministic workflow replay from event history; activities, signals/updates for approvals, child workflows for fan-out; AI integrations for OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI, Google ADK, Strands, Vercel AI SDK, Spring AI; Replit migrated its coding agent to Temporal. License: MIT (22,820 stars). Pricing (docs.temporal.io/cloud/pricing): Essentials greater of $100/mo or 5% of usage (1M Actions, 1 GB active, 40 GB retained storage); Business greater of $500/mo or 10% (2.5M Actions); Enterprise and Mission Critical annual; pay-as-you-go $50 per million Actions for the first 5M, stepping to $25/M above 100M; active storage $0.042/GBh, retained $0.00105/GBh. EU regions: AWS Frankfurt, Ireland, London; GCP Frankfurt; EU regions replicate to each other. Reverse-engineer: the "Action" as the single metered unit (every persisted state transition), which makes the cost of a step-level audit trail predictable and forces side effects into idempotent activities.

**Inngest — Inngest, Inc.** Event-driven durable functions where each `step.run` is memoized; `step.waitForEvent` gives human gates; concurrency keys throttle fan-out; AgentKit (Apache-2.0, 926 stars) adds deterministic multi-agent routing. License: server under SSPL v1.0 converting to Apache-2.0 after three years (5,805 stars). Pricing (inngest.com/pricing): Hobby $0 with 50k executions/mo, 5 concurrent steps, 24-hour history; Pro from $99/mo with 1M executions, 100 concurrent steps then $25 per 25, 7-day history, 15 users then $10/user, $0.50 per million events beyond 5M, $3/GB spans beyond 5 GB; Enterprise custom with 90-day history. An execution is the run plus each step. Reverse-engineer: billing and concurrency expressed in *steps*, and concurrency keys scoped by arbitrary expression (per tenant, per repo) rather than global worker counts.

**Restate — Restate Software.** Journal-based durable execution with virtual objects and awakeables for external/human completion; "Durable Agents" patterns record every agent step so a crashed agent resumes exactly. License: BSL 1.1, converting to Apache-2.0 four years after each release; production use allowed except operating a managed service that exposes Restate's APIs (4,376 stars). Pricing (restate.dev/pricing): Free $0 with 100k actions, 10 actions/s, 1-day retention; Starter $75/mo with 5M actions, 50 actions/s (burst 500), 3-day retention; Business $300/mo with 20M actions, 200 actions/s, 20 GB, 7-day retention; Premium $1,000/mo with 50M actions, 500 actions/s, 30-day retention; overage $25/M ($15/M Premium); HIPAA BAA +$300, multi-AZ +$200/+$500; 99.9% SLA. Cloud regions not stated. Reverse-engineer: the durable promise/awakeable — a step yields an ID, an external system (human, CI) completes it later, and the journal makes the wait free.

**DBOS — DBOS, Inc.** Library-level durable workflows checkpointed in Postgres (SQLite locally); Conductor UI adds distributed recovery, versioning and fork-from-step. License: MIT (Python SDK 1,559 stars). Pricing (dbos.dev/dbos-pricing): Pro $99/mo (2 seats, 3 apps, 1M checkpoints/mo, $50 per extra million); Teams $499/mo (10 seats, 10 apps, 10M checkpoints, $40/M, RBAC, SOC2/HIPAA); Enterprise custom with SSO and self-hosted, air-gapped Conductor. Reverse-engineer: fork a workflow from step N with edited inputs — the cheapest way to A/B a single step variant against an already-recorded prefix.

**Ray / Anyscale — Anyscale, Inc.** Ray is the distributed compute layer (tasks, actors, object store) used for massive fan-out; Anyscale is managed Ray. License: Apache-2.0 (43,700 stars). Pricing (anyscale.com/pricing): pay-as-you-go platform credits — CPU-only $0.0135/hour, T4 $0.5682, L4 $0.9542, A10G $1.3635, A100 $4.9591, H/B/GB families quote; Hosted (limited regions) or BYOC (any cloud/region/on-prem); $100 free credits. License: Apache-2.0 (744 stars). Pricing: free; Diagrid's managed offerings quote-based. Reverse-engineer: per-agent SPIFFE identity so tool authorization is tied to the agent, not the host.

License: Apache-2.0 (3,647 stars); CNCF maturity level not stated in the README. Pricing: free; enterprise quote. Reverse-engineer: agents as declarative Kubernetes resources so GitOps owns rollout and rollback of agent definitions.

## 4. Research on multi-agent effectiveness and failure (2025–2026)

- **MAST — "Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?"** (Cemri et al., arXiv 2503.13657 v3, 26 Oct 2025; NeurIPS 2025 poster). 1,642 annotated traces across ChatDev, MetaGPT, HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2 (MathChat), Magentic-One, OpenManus; 14 failure modes in three categories — system design (FM-1.1 disobey task spec 11.8%, FM-1.3 step repetition 15.7%, FM-1.5 unaware of stopping conditions 12.4%), inter-agent misalignment (FM-2.6 reasoning–action mismatch 13.2%, FM-2.3 task derailment 7.4%), task verification (FM-3.3 incorrect verification 9.1%, FM-3.2 no/incomplete verification 8.2%). Human κ = 0.88; LLM-as-judge pipeline 94% accuracy, κ 0.77. Interventions on ChatDev: enforcing final approval by the CEO agent +9.4%, adding a high-level objective verification step +15.6% on ProgramDev. Implication for Daliesk: verification is a workflow step with its own score, not a prompt line.
- **Anthropic, "How we built our multi-agent research system"** (13 June 2025). Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on an internal research eval; token usage explains 80% of BrowseComp variance (95% with tool calls and model choice); agents use ~4× and multi-agent ~15× the tokens of chat; 3–5 subagents with 3+ parallel tool calls cut research time up to 90%; production used rainbow deployments, checkpoint-based resumption and full tracing; LLM-as-judge rubrics plus human review.
- **Anthropic, "Building multi-agent systems: when and how to use them"** (23 Jan 2026). Multi-agent helps for context protection, parallelization and specialization; "3–10× more tokens than single-agent approaches for equivalent tasks"; teams "invest months building elaborate multi-agent architectures only to discover that improved prompting on a single agent achieved equivalent results".
- **Google Research, "Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems"** (Kim & Liu, arXiv 2512.08296; blog 28 Jan 2026). 180 configurations, five architectures, four benchmarks, three model families: +81% on parallelizable Finance-Agent with coordination; 39–70% degradation on sequential PlanCraft for every multi-agent variant; independent multi-agent systems amplify errors 17.2× vs 4.4× with centralized coordination; a predictive model picks the right architecture for 87% of unseen tasks.
- **Microsoft.** Conductor (14 May 2026, MIT): deterministic YAML routing. Agent Framework 1.0 GA (3 Apr 2026) ships Magentic orchestration; Foundry reports procedural memory gains of 7–14 percentage points (Build, 2 June 2026). No Microsoft ICLR/NeurIPS 2026 orchestration paper was verified.
- **2026 framework/orchestration benchmarks.** *Open Agent Specification* (Oracle, 19 May 2026): identical agent specs run on LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen and WayFlow diverge — τ²-Bench AutoGen 73.5% vs CrewAI 62.5%; SimpleQA Verified CrewAI 81.1% vs WayFlow 79.0%; BIRD-SQL ~54% everywhere. *OrchestraBench* (5 Aug 2026): failure-injection harness; keyword routers scored 0% on adversarial routing vs 100% for intent-reasoning routers; tool faults recover fully, ambiguous delegation 0.30, latent semantic failures 0.0; cascade radius grows from 0.9 to 4.7 as pipeline depth goes 3→7. *"Resume Means Resume"* (arXiv 2608.03836, Aug 2026): a machine-checked RESUME CONTRACT (prefix continuation, effect exactly-once, fork determinism, checkpoint validity, consume-once, recovery determinism) shows LangGraph 1.2.9 re-executes durably recorded work after SIGKILL, CrewAI 1.15.2 re-executes completed methods, pydantic-graph cannot resume mid-node, and k concurrent resumers fire a gated effect k times in 36 of 40 cells. *Scaling Behavior of Single-LLM-Driven MAS* (30 May 2026): diminishing returns from coordination overhead, not context length. *Who Broke the System?* (COLM 2026) and *Adaptive Influence Graphs* (Aug 2026): failure attribution to agent and step is now a benchmarked task. *Compiling Agentic Workflows into LLM Weights* (21 May 2026): claims near-frontier quality at ~100× lower cost by fine-tuning a small model on a 14–55-node workflow, and counts >290k GitHub stars across LangGraph, CrewAI, ADK, OpenAI Agents SDK, Semantic Kernel, Strands and LlamaIndex.

## 5. (a) Ranked shortlist for a 300-agent workflow with per-step scoring

1. **Temporal (self-hosted, MIT) + Langfuse (self-hosted or EU cloud, MIT)** — deterministic replay, signal-based approvals, unbounded fan-out, EU sovereignty, and per-observation scores at the lowest verified platform cost. Gap: build the evaluator and A/B layer yourself (Daliesk plugins as Temporal workers).
2. **AWS Bedrock AgentCore (Frankfurt/Ireland/Stockholm/Paris)** — the only managed observe→evaluate→A/B→optimize loop that is GA, framework-agnostic and EU-resident; no self-hosting; token-priced evaluators dominate cost if every step is scored.
3. **LangGraph + LangSmith (EU cloud)** — best step-level feedback tooling and largest ecosystem; caveats: resume-semantics defects reported for 1.2.9, self-hosting only on Enterprise, unclear LSU trace pricing.
4. **Microsoft Agent Framework + Durable Task / Foundry hosted agents (Sweden Central, Germany West Central)** — checkpointing and HITL are first-class; Agent Optimizer still preview; A/B not verified.
5. **Anthropic Managed Agents / Claude Agent SDK** — outcome rubric grading and 25-thread multiagent sessions are the most "verification-first" primitives, but scoring is per outcome, the control plane is not EU-resident, and there is no ZDR.
6. **Restate, DBOS, Inngest** — lighter durable engines; DBOS's Postgres-only checkpoints and fork-from-step fit a plugin harness well; watch BSL/SSPL terms.
7. **Google ADK 2.0 + Agent Engine** — strong eval tooling and graph runtime; EU region availability unverified in this pass.
8. **Dapr Agents / kagent** — Kubernetes-native durability and identity; no eval layer.
9. **Prefect / Airflow 3.3** — scheduled orchestration with HITL operators; no LLM-step scoring.
10. **n8n / Dify** — concurrency caps and low-code limits; Flowise is archived.

## 5. (b) Cost model: 300 agents × 1 run/day × 30 days, 50 steps per agent, traces retained 90 days

Assumptions: 9,000 agent runs/month; 450,000 steps; each step = one model call + one tool call (~3 spans/step → 1.35M spans/month) and one score (450k scores); ~40k input tokens per step average → ~72 GB of logged prompt/response text per month, ~216 GB retained at 90 days; each run occupies 1 vCPU/2 GiB for one hour (9,000 vCPU-h, 18,000 GiB-h); peak concurrency 300. Platform fees only, list prices, 5 seats where seat-priced.

Model tokens (separate): 2M input + 200k output per run, 9,000 runs → 18B input, 1.8B output tokens/month. Claude Opus 5 ($5/$25): $15/run → **$135,000/month**; with 80% cache reads (0.1×) ≈ $70,200. Claude Sonnet 5 ($2/$10): $6/run → **$54,000/month**; cached ≈ $28,080. Platform fees below are 0.1–3% of token spend.
